title: Per-Iteration Scope: Fresh Environment for Each Loop Body
description: Each iteration pushes a child environment. Variables defined inside vanish after the iteration, while assign to outer variables still works.

steps.description: The Environment class with define, lookup, assign, and __repr__ for chain visualization.
glob defines n as 4 to drive the loop.
The while loop runs as long as n is greater than 0, with iteration counting each pass.
Each iteration creates a new loop_env, defines t as n times 2, then prints t and n visible from the loop.

steps.question: What happens when we try glob.lookup('t') after the loop

steps.description: n is updated with assign, which walks the chain to glob and decrements n.
After the loop, n is 0 in glob, and t is gone because it was only defined in per-iteration scopes.
Running prints four iterations with t = 8, 6, 4, 2, then After loop: n = 0, and After loop: t is gone -- undefined variable 't'.
